title: Sciencese: Learning Science as a Second Language Through Drama Pedagogy
content: Scientific literacy can be understood as participation in the communicative practices through which scientific knowledge is constructed rather than as the acquisition of disciplinary concepts alone. Building on this perspective, we propose the concept of Sciencese, an epistemic language that integrates the semiotic, representational, and social resources through which science is practiced. This reframing raises a central educational question: if scientific literacy develops through acquiring fluency in Sciencese, what can science education learn from theories of Second Language Acquisition (SLA)? To address this question, we develop a conceptual synthesis connecting three research traditions rarely examined within a common framework: science education, SLA, and Drama Pedagogy (DP). We argue that contemporary SLA identifies learning mechanisms—including meaningful input, interaction, productive communication, embodiment, identity formation, and psychologically safe experimentation—that are equally fundamental to learning science. Rather than viewing DP primarily as an artistic methodology, we interpret it as a pedagogical ecology that naturally integrates these mechanisms. From this synthesis, we propose the Pedagogical Translation Framework, which shifts pedagogical transfer from instructional techniques to underlying learning mechanisms. Instead of advocating theatrical activities in science classrooms, the framework explains how drama-based pedagogies reveal transferable principles that can inform diverse forms of science instruction. We illustrate this perspective through two complementary implementation pathways: a drama-centered model based on artistic creation and a science-centered model that embeds performative interventions within conventional teaching. By conceptualizing scientific literacy as the progressive acquisition of fluency in Sciencese, this article offers an integrative theoretical framework linking science education and language education while providing a general model for translating pedagogical knowledge across disciplinary boundaries.
